newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Budget cut to ease rate pressure - Australia PM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Budget cut to ease rate pressure - Australia PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday he hoped the government's efforts to reduce the budget deficit would ease pressure on interest rates.
"When I talk about the desirability of budget deficits being lower, I have in mind lower interest rates," Howard told reporters.

"When I argue for wage restraint, I have in mind lower interest rates because of the feed-in effect of wage restraint on inflation rates, and when we argue for trade liberalisation we are talking about job generation and job creation," he said.

In its August 20 budget, Howard's conservative government announced budget cuts of A$7.2 billion over two years and Treasurer Peter Costello has said the government would decide in 1997 on whether any further measures would be taken.
The government promised A$8.0 billion in cuts over two years soon after it won the March 2 election.
It is currently forecasting a A$5.6 billion underlying deficit in the year to June 30, 1997, a A$1.5 billion deficit in 1997/98, and a A$1.0 billion surplus in 1998/99.
